findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 11 in the same format as Chapter 1 (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 12 questions numbered 1-12; by section: 11.1 2, 11.3 6, 11.4 2, 11.5 2.

6 pairs (theory 5 marks + numerical 3 marks) covering relative motion (the dropped-ball experiment), the postulates with time dilation, length contraction, mass variation, mass-energy equivalence, and simultaneity with the hypothetical spaceship journey. The chapter states its equations without derivation, so the theory answers follow the book's explanation and equations. Numericals use new values, recomputed in Python. Book corrections followed: no material object moves at c.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
